text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000014 bills 99215 at roughly three times the risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity stratum, including low-complexity patients, but only one 99215 claim has documentation, so the records cannot confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The by-complexity table shows the elevated 99215 share is not explained by a sicker panel. The excess appears at every condition count, including the 0 and 1 condition groups. Sampled low-complexity 99215 claims sit on routine diagnoses such as UTI (C0009167), upper respiratory infection (C0009328), follow-up visits (C0009183, C0010234) and abdominal pain (C0010288), which is the pattern consistent with upcoding that warrants concern. The documentation does not settle the question: only one documented 99215 exists (C0010217, supported at high MDM), and the one below-billed note (C0010179) is a 99214. A few notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed had no lab or test line on the claim, which is weak evidence of templated or inflated notes, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet, then check whether MDM and data-reviewed entries in those charts reflect actual work or cloned templates."}
